summary: Bear River light, a 1905 wooden tower on Winchester Point in Nova Scotia, was decommissioned in 2001; restoration by a local society began in 2022.

events.note: Wooden tower built by contract for $494; reported in the Chief Engineer's section for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1905
Put in operation 1 May 1905; fixed red dioptric light, seventh order
William Hunt appointed first keeper, 10 April 1905 (LighthouseFriends)
H.B. Warren appointed keeper when Hunt left in 1913 (LighthouseFriends prose); LighthouseFriends' roster starts Warren in 1914
Digby Town Council votes (14 December 2009) to acquire the lighthouse; the transfer was delayed for many years
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse, 15 February 2015
Ownership passes to the Municipality of Digby, spring 2021
Restoration of the tower starts, August 2022

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says it was decommissioned as a navigational aid in 2001; the Lighthouse Directory says 'Inactive since 2001'. Smith's Cove Historical Society gives the same 2001 date.

The 1905 report gives 72 ft (21.9 m) above high water. Digby's 2022 registration gives 69 ft. The record's 20.0 m (about 66 ft) matches neither; a human should check the current CCG figure before changing it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record carries a conflict that sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The sources I read all date its decommissioning to 2001: LighthouseFriends, the Smith's Cove society and the Lighthouse Directory. The NSLPS page says only that the tower is still standing, which is about the structure, not the light.
The 1905 report gives 72 ft above high water and Digby's 2022 registration gives 69 ft. The story uses the 1905 figure and says that the two differ.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27: all 40 quotes were found on the first run. Story changes: 'small' removed (no source), the register's warning of shoals is now a statement of what the register says, not the reason it was built; 'supported' changed to 'supported the development of' as the register words it; the 45 ft and 100 ft ground heights and the 69 ft registration height are now metres first; The place is a separate chapter, so the register statement and the open-area line are no longer under Building the light. Page checks: the 1905 report p. 29 is scan p. 34 (checked against corpus.py page); the 1906 keeper statement p. 172 is scan p. 181 (checked). The 'Hunt, Wm Bear River April' line is matched by position in one OCR line; the page image at scan p. 181 was NOT viewed by the checker, so a human should confirm Hunt's line. LighthouseFriends corroborates Hunt at Bear River independently. Warren's appointment is 1913 in LighthouseFriends' prose and 1914 in its roster; the story says 1913 and the JSON event now matches. Earlier note: Matched by position in OCR: the 1906 keeper list (source 7, scan p.181) prints the name Hunt, Wm beside Bear River, and the appointment date columns are split from the names in the OCR, so I did not match Hunt's date to the column. The April 1905 date and the $150 salary come from LighthouseFriends only. Please check the image at scan p.181 for Hunt's line. Contractor: the 1905 report's OCR reads 'John Honey, of Granville Ferry'; LighthouseFriends prints 'John Roney'. The story does not name him. Check the image at scan p.34 before any name is used. Warren (1914 to at least 1923) comes only from LighthouseFriends; I could not find him in the corpus keeper lists for 1912 to 1924. Later keepers, if any, are not sourced. Light: the 1905 report gives 'miles', not nautical miles, so the story says 'nine miles' as the report does. The record's 'active' status is contradicted by three sources. The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights (NOTMAR) page is a script page that did not return the Bear River line, so the current listing is unverified. The Parks Canada DFHD page returned no text (script-only), so the story uses the Canadian Register text as reproduced by Heritage Guide. Access: LighthouseFriends gives a dirt lane off Route 1 with parking; the Lighthouse Directory gives a walk of about 1 km from the Digby County Rail Trail. The story uses only the tower-closed and grounds-open statement. Storms, wrecks and rescues: nothing dated was found for this station. The 1915 and 1921 Chief Engineer's entries for Bear River concern river clearing and a wrecked bridge, not the light, so they are left out. The 'Smith's Cove Historical Society' and the 'Bear River Lighthouse Society' are both named for the same care role in LighthouseFriends; the story names the 2002 society only as LighthouseFriends does. A 1992 NSLPS light-details line ('7th order dioptric lens, electric lantern') is not used because it does not say what happened in 1992.
